name: Live small-group classes for kids on Outschool
summary: Design and teach live or self-paced classes for ages 3-18; parents pay per class and Outschool keeps 30%.
howItWorks: You list a class (one-off, multi-week, ongoing weekly or self-paced) on a topic kids or homeschooling parents want, set the price and group size, and teach live over Outschool's video tool. Parents find classes through Outschool search and pay up front. Outschool takes a 30% teacher fee and pays you 70%; parents also pay a separate marketplace fee. Ongoing weekly classes create recurring income once a class gets reviews.

payout.notes: Outschool keeps 30% and pays 70% of the class price, always in USD. Upfront fixed-length classes pay 7-8 days after the start date; weekly classes are processed on Sundays 7-13 days after the meetings; self-paced pay-in-full pays 7-8 days after enrollment. No minimum payout is stated. As of Nov 2026 the move to Stripe is still rolling out: Outschool says payouts 'continue through PayPal for now', with no fixed end date for PayPal. Stripe payouts will go to banks in the approved teaching countries.

legality.notes: Teaching children online is legal everywhere; child-safeguarding rules and Outschool's background check apply.

availability.notes: Teachers must be full-time residents of the US, Mexico, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Spain or the UK. Of the 50 reference countries only US, CA, MX, UK, AU and KR qualify (about 12%).

automationPlan: Use AI to draft class outlines, slides, worksheets and listing copy
Template class listings and auto-reply messages to parents
Self-paced classes reuse recorded lessons with no live time
manualSteps: Teaching every live session on camera
fullCycle: Teach first sections and collect reviews
Get paid via PayPal (Stripe once migrated) to bank
risks: New listings get little search traffic
Kids' class demand is seasonal (school breaks)
evidence: Outschool's help center sets out the 70/30 split and the payout schedules for each enrollment type. It is a large US kids' class marketplace with many full-time educators.

tools: LLM free tier for lesson plans
skills: designing a 4-8 week class outline (AI can draft)
accounts: Outschool educator account + ID verification + background check

unitEconomics.notes: Typical Outschool listings charge about $10-25 per learner per 45-55 min meeting (estimate from listings); Outschool keeps 30%. Hours assume ~4 learners per meeting plus prep.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; 'break-even' is the first paid class, usually 1-2 months after approval because new listings get little search traffic.

marketConditions.notes: Demand has fallen from the 2020-21 peak and established teachers with hundreds of reviews and ongoing weekly classes take most bookings. Only 8 teaching countries are eligible. AI helps with prep but does not replace a live adult teacher for kids. Main failure mode: classes that never fill past 1-2 learners and get cancelled. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $250 to $80 so it agrees with the 30% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch at or slightly below the category median (about $10-12 per meeting) with a one-time intro class to collect reviews, then raise to $15-20 and push learners into ongoing weekly classes.
profitPath: Month 0: approval, background check and 3 class listings (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first one-time classes with 1-3 learners, about $50-150/month
Month 3-6: convert best-reviewed topic into an ongoing weekly class; $200-400/month
Month 6-12: add sections at peak times and a self-paced version; $300-1,000/month for those who stick

name: Live music, art and language lessons on Lessonface
summary: Teach live online lessons and group classes in music, arts and languages through a lessons marketplace that charges a low fee for students you bring yourself.
howItWorks: Lessonface is a public-benefit marketplace for live online lessons, mostly music (voice, guitar, violin, piano), plus art, dance and language. You set your own rates and schedule. Students found by Lessonface cost 15%, students you refer cost 5%, and group classes, self-paced courses and downloadables cost up to 30%. Its booking, payments and video room make it a full back office for your own students, while the marketplace adds new ones.

payout.notes: Lessonface's Teacher Payments page says PayPal payouts go out weekly on Fridays, and the teacher pays PayPal's fees. The first payment takes about a week, then usually 2-3 days. Direct deposit is for US bank accounts only and is closed to new teachers. Lessons not acknowledged within 4 weeks are forfeited (third-party report). Fees: 15% for students Lessonface finds, 5% for students you bring, up to 30% for classes, courses and downloadables sold to Lessonface-referred students. These Lessonface pages block automated fetches; the figures come from their indexed text.

legality.notes: Teaching is legal everywhere; a background check applies.
complianceRequirements: teaching experience (2+ years) or 5 years professional experience

availability.notes: Payouts run through PayPal, so they reach most reference countries where PayPal can receive money (not e.g. Bangladesh, Iraq, Libya or Tunisia). Lessonface lists teachers outside the US, but it has no official list of countries it accepts teachers from.

automationPlan: AI-generated practice sheets, lesson notes and progress summaries
Automated booking reminders and package renewals
Reuse recorded material as self-paced courses
fullCycle: Receive weekly PayPal payout and withdraw to bank
risks: Small marketplace with limited inbound demand
Payout only via PayPal for new teachers (PayPal fees, no PayPal receiving in some countries)
evidence: Lessonface's teaching and recruiting pages give 15% fees for marketplace students, 5% for teacher-referred students and up to 30% for classes and courses. Its Teacher Payments page documents weekly PayPal payouts. Its 2020 year-in-review describes an active teacher base.

skills: teaching an instrument, voice, art or language at a real level

unitEconomics.notes: Rates are set by the teacher; $30-80 per lesson matches Lessonface music listings (estimate). 15% fee for Lessonface-found students (5% for your own), plus ~$2 PayPal fee. Fee figures are estimated: lessonface.com/fees is bot-blocked and could not be re-checked.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; first paid lesson usually arrives in 1-3 months because the marketplace is small.

marketConditions.notes: Online music lessons are a steady niche; teachers who already have students and use Lessonface as their back office (5% fee) earn the most. Inbound demand from the marketplace is limited, so most newcomers get only a few students. AI apps compete for beginners but not for skilled feedback on technique. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $150 to $60 so it agrees with the 25% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Offer a discounted first lesson and 4-lesson package near $35-40, then move to $45-60 once you have reviews; bring existing students in to pay only 5%.
profitPath: Month 0: profile, intro video, rate card (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first 1-3 students, about $50-200/month
Month 3-6: packages plus your own students moved onto the 5% tier; $200-500/month
Month 6-12: group classes or downloadables; $300-1,000/month for active teachers

name: Lead-generation tutoring listings (Superprof, Apprentus) with direct student payment
summary: List free on a tutor directory where students pay the platform for access and you collect lesson fees yourself, with 0-10% commission.
howItWorks: Unlike commission marketplaces, Superprof charges students a 'Student Pass' to contact tutors and lets tutors list for free. Tutors set their price and either take payment directly (bank transfer, PayPal, Wise; 0% commission) or through Superprof (10% commission, or 0% on a paid Premium account). Apprentus works the same way in Europe, with a fee on the first lesson. You get a lead, run a trial, then keep the student long-term on your own terms.

methods: direct from student: bank transfer / PayPal / Wise
payout.notes: With direct payment you control the timing. Superprof's own blog confirms the 10% commission on in-platform payments (0% with Premium) but gives no Premium price and no in-platform payout method or timing. A complaint-forum post says earnings show about 24 hours after a lesson and reach PayPal in about 3 days; this is unverified. Official Superprof help and FAQ pages block automated fetches.

legality.notes: Private tutoring is legal everywhere. Some countries require registering as self-employed or for VAT above thresholds.

availability.notes: Superprof runs local sites in dozens of countries (e.g. .com, .co.uk, .fr, .com.br, .com.mx, .co.in, .ca, .com.au). Students pay you directly, so payout works almost anywhere.

automationPlan: AI-drafted profile, lesson plans and homework
Booking via Calendly/Cal.com and invoicing via Stripe/Wise
Auto-reply templates for incoming leads
manualSteps: Profile with photo and ID verification
risks: Students pay a pass, so lead volume can be thin
Collecting payment yourself carries non-payment risk
Rival platforms say Superprof has hidden fees; read the terms for your country
evidence: Superprof's own blog says listing is free, gives the 10% commission (0% with Premium or off-platform payment), and says it has millions of registered tutors.

skills: subject expertise (school maths, languages, music, etc.)
accounts: PayPal / Wise / bank for direct payment

unitEconomics.notes: Tutors set rates; $15-60/hour reflects typical Superprof listings across countries (estimate). Direct payment = 0% commission; in-platform payment is 10%. Cost covers payment fees. Superprof confirms 10% on in-platform payments and 0% with a Premium account.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; first student often within 2-8 weeks, but lead volume varies sharply by country and subject.

marketConditions.notes: Exam-prep and language tutors with strong reviews keep winning; homework-help demand is being eroded by free AI tutors since 2024-25. Superprof's student pass limits leads, and many listings compete on the same subject. Failure modes: no contacts for weeks, and students who stop after 2-3 lessons or do not pay. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $250 to $80 so it agrees with the 35% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Offer a free or discounted first lesson (common on Superprof) at about 20% below the local median, then raise rates after 10 reviews and sell prepaid 5-10 lesson packages.
profitPath: Month 0: listings on Superprof and Apprentus, set direct-payment terms (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first 1-2 students, about $100-200/month
Month 3-6: 4-6 regular students via reviews and referrals; $300-600/month
Month 6-12: raise rates, sell packages; $400-1,500/month for those who stick

name: Agency-assigned tutoring as a contractor (GoStudent, Varsity Tutors)
summary: Tutor school students that a tutoring company matches to you, at a per-session rate the company sets. The company handles acquisition, parents and billing.
howItWorks: Tutoring companies sell lesson subscriptions to parents and assign the students to freelance tutors. You don't market yourself or set prices. You take students in your subjects, teach on the company's classroom tool and log sessions. GoStudent (Europe) pays a base rate of up to GBP 16 per 50-minute lesson, with volume raises (+1.00 per lesson after 150 lessons in 6 months, +1.50 after 300). Varsity Tutors (US) pays per session twice a week.

payout.minimumPayout: No minimum (GoStudent); Varsity Tutors not stated
payout.notes: GoStudent's tutor help center: base rate up to GBP 16 per 50-minute session, depending on availability, subjects and monthly sessions completed. Earnings are paid in full the next month with no minimum, between the 12th and 17th; transfers can take up to 7 days to arrive. Session feedback must be submitted within 24 hours or the session is not paid. No-shows pay a flat 6.50. Volume raises: +1.00 per lesson after 150 lessons in 6 months, +1.50 after 300. Varsity Tutors' twice-weekly pay and USD 15-40/hr come only from third-party sources; its tutor pages block automated fetches.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you are an independent contractor and handle your own tax.

availability.notes: GoStudent runs sites for the UK, DE, AT, FR, IT, ES, TR, PL, NL and GR and says anyone over 18 can apply, but it names no residence rule. Varsity Tutors contracts with US residents only and reportedly excludes several US states (unverified).

automationPlan: AI-prepared lesson plans and practice sets per student
Session-notes templates
Calendar automation
risks: Low per-hour pay compared with independent tutoring
evidence: GoStudent's tutor help center documents the base rate, the monthly pay cycle with no minimum and the volume raises. Varsity Tutors is run by a public company (Nerdy) with many contractor postings, but its pay terms could not be checked on an official page.

skills: passing a demo lesson and interview
accounts: GoStudent or Varsity Tutors contractor account

unitEconomics.notes: Agency sets pay: GoStudent up to GBP 16 per 50-min session (about $21) plus volume bonuses; Varsity Tutors $15-40/hr is third-party reported. Agency margin is already deducted.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; first pay arrives the month after your first sessions (GoStudent pays the 12th-17th).

marketConditions.notes: The agency finds and assigns students, so accepted tutors almost always get paid; the limit is low hourly pay and eligibility in only a few countries. AI homework help reduces demand for basic subjects, while exam prep holds up. Failure modes: unpaid sessions after missed feedback deadlines, fines for no-shows, and few assigned students in low-demand subjects.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Pay is fixed by the agency; maximise it by offering peak evening slots, high-demand subjects and enough volume to hit the 150/300-lesson bonuses.
profitPath: Month 0: apply, interview, demo lesson, onboarding (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first assigned students, about $100-300/month
Month 3-6: 15-25 sessions/month, about $300-500/month
Month 6-12: volume bonus tier and more students; $500-1,000/month part-time

name: Freelance teacher at an online language school with a set curriculum (Lingoda)
summary: Teach small-group or 1:1 language classes from a school's ready-made curriculum for a fixed per-class fee. The school supplies the students and materials.
howItWorks: Online language schools such as Lingoda sell subscriptions and need certified teachers to run scheduled Zoom classes from their CEFR-aligned materials. You choose time slots, the school fills them, and you teach without writing a curriculum or finding students. Unlike Preply or italki you don't set prices or compete on a marketplace. Lingoda wants C2 language level, a teaching certificate and 2-3 years of experience, and runs on freelance contracts.

payout.notes: Lingoda's jobs page confirms the freelance model and says teachers are 'paid on time'; its teacher-referral page (Nov 2026) confirms teachers are paid via a monthly teaching invoice. Still unconfirmed: the per-class pay rate (third-party sources report about USD 8-13 per hour or EUR 11 per class), the payment method (bank transfer assumed) and any minimum payout.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; freelancers must be legally able to invoice in their country.

availability.notes: Job listings say 'Remote - all countries' as long as you can legally freelance. Some languages require native-level skill.

automationPlan: AI-generated warm-ups and extra practice
Reusable class notes
Calendar sync for slot booking
evidence: Lingoda's official jobs page confirms the freelance model and requirements and describes a teacher-relations team that 'ensures every teacher is paid on time'.

tools: school-provided Zoom classes and CEFR materials

unitEconomics.notes: Lingoda does not publish pay (its jobs page gives no rate); TEFL.org reports about $8-13 (GBP 6.33-10.30) per hour-long class, so $8-13 is estimated and unverified.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. Assumes you already hold the required certificate; if not, a TEFL course costs $150-1,500 and should be counted as startup cash.

marketConditions.notes: For qualified teachers this is reliable but low-paid work. AI conversation apps and cheaper marketplace tutors pressure language-school subscriptions in 2025-26, which reduces open slots. Failure modes: rejection for missing credentials, class cancellations and slots not filling. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $400 to $90 so it agrees with the 40% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing control; increase income by offering popular time slots, multiple levels and high reliability scores.
profitPath: Month 0: application, demo, contract (cost $0 if already certified)
Month 1-2: first classes, about $100-300/month
Month 3-6: 30-40 classes/month, about $350-500/month
Month 6-12: steady part-time schedule; $400-1,000/month

name: Author a produced course for a curated publisher (LinkedIn Learning, Pluralsight, Domestika)
summary: Pitch and audition to make a course that the platform produces and distributes. You get paid by the publisher through fees and/or royalties, not per student sale.
howItWorks: Curated course publishers recruit experts by application. LinkedIn Learning wants a teaching video sample and proposal. Pluralsight asks for an audition video, and its video-course pay is partly based on viewership, paid quarterly. Domestika covers production for creative courses and pays via PayPal. Once accepted, the publisher handles editing, marketing and enterprise distribution. That's different from self-publishing on Udemy or Skillshare.

methods: per contract (LinkedIn Learning/Pluralsight; method not published)
payout.notes: Pluralsight's teach page says video-course pay is 'partially based on viewership' and paid quarterly. Domestika's page says you need a verified PayPal account and that it covers production costs. LinkedIn Learning's instructor page says only 'earn extra income'. None of the three publish royalty percentages, upfront fees or minimums; terms are set in the individual contract.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you sign an IP license/assignment contract.
complianceRequirements: contract with IP assignment or license

availability.notes: Applications are open worldwide (LinkedIn teaching languages: EN, DE, ES, FR, JA, PT-BR, ZH). Acceptance is selective and favors recognized experts.

automationPlan: AI-drafted outlines, scripts and exercise files
Automated screen-recording and caption cleanup
Pitch templates for multiple publishers
fullCycle: Apply with proposal and sample video
evidence: Official instructor pages for LinkedIn Learning, Pluralsight (quarterly viewership payments) and Domestika (PayPal, production covered) confirm the programs are open to apply.

skills: recognised expertise in a business, tech or creative topic
writing a course proposal and audition video
accounts: LinkedIn Learning / Pluralsight / Domestika instructor application

unitEconomics.notes: Publishers do not publish rates; $1k-15k per course in the first year is an estimate from instructor accounts (upfront fee and/or royalties). Figures are author receipts after the publisher's share.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; most applicants are not accepted, and accepted authors usually wait 6-12 months from proposal to first payment.

marketConditions.notes: Enterprise learning libraries have cut new commissions and refreshed catalogues as AI-generated and AI-assisted training spreads in 2025-26. Known experts with existing audiences get accepted; average applicants are not. Failure modes: rejection, exclusivity clauses and courses retired after a few years.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Terms are set by contract; negotiate a higher upfront fee where available and keep rights to repurpose material elsewhere.
profitPath: Month 0: proposal and audition video to 2-3 publishers (cost $0)
Month 1-4: if accepted, script and record with publisher (no pay yet)
Month 5-9: course published; first fee or quarterly royalty, $500-3,000
Month 9-12: pitch a second course or update; most earn $0-200/month averaged

name: Paid online exam marking for international exam boards (IB, Cambridge International)
summary: Qualified teachers mark scanned exam scripts online during exam sessions, paid per script or component by the exam board.
howItWorks: International exam boards hire seasonal examiners to mark IB Diploma, IGCSE and A Level papers. Scripts are scanned and marked on screen (e.g. RM Assessor), so you can work from home in many countries. You pass standardization, mark your allocation by the deadline and get paid per script. Experienced examiners move up to team leader, setter, item writer or moderator roles. The payer is the exam board, not students.

payout.notes: Cambridge International's examiner FAQ says assessment specialists are usually paid GBP 1.00-5.00 per script, depending on syllabus and script type, and that travel to required meetings is reimbursed. It does not state payment method or timing. IB pages block automated fetches, so IB fees, payment method and timing are unverified.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; contractor fees are taxable.

availability.notes: Recruitment is worldwide for many subjects; some roles require teaching the syllabus. Unverified per country.

automationPlan: Keep mark schemes and standardization notes organized
Calendar reminders for marking windows
manualSteps: Marking every script by hand (AI marking is not allowed)
risks: Pay per script can be low
evidence: Cambridge International publicly recruits assistant examiners, team leaders, setters, item writers and moderators via assessors.cambridge.org, and its FAQ gives GBP 1-5 per script. The IB runs a global examiner network.

tools: RM Assessor or board's on-screen marking tool (provided)
skills: degree and teaching background in the subject
equipment: laptop or desktop with large screen
accounts: examiner contract with Cambridge International or IB

unitEconomics.notes: Cambridge International pays GBP 1-5 per script (about $1.3-6.5) depending on syllabus; IB fees are unverified. Roughly 5 scripts/hour for mid-length papers.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; income comes in two seasonal bursts (May/June and Oct/Nov), so first pay can be 2-8 months after applying.

marketConditions.notes: Boards regularly recruit examiners, and qualified teachers who pass standardisation are reliably paid. Income is lumpy: a session can pay $500-2,000, which averages to $100-300/month. AI-assisted marking is being trialled but does not yet replace human examiners. Failure modes: no allocation in your subject, failing standardisation, and burnout at deadline time. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $250 to $60 so it agrees with the 25% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Fees are fixed; raise earnings by taking larger allocations, marking several syllabuses and moving up to team leader or setter roles.
profitPath: Month 0: apply to Cambridge and IB with subject credentials (cost $0)
Month 1-6: training and standardisation before the next session
First session: mark 300-500 scripts, $1,000-2,000 paid after the session
Month 6-12: second session plus senior-role applications; averages $150-300/month

name: Sell an online course through Hotmart's built-in affiliate network
summary: Publish a course or digital training on Hotmart and let its marketplace of affiliates promote it for a commission you set.
howItWorks: Hotmart is a Brazil-born creator platform for courses and digital products, strongest in Latin America and Europe. You host the course in its member area, set the price and an affiliate commission, and list it in the affiliate marketplace. There, thousands of affiliates choose products to promote with their own traffic. That differs from Teachable or Udemy because sales can come from other people's marketing. Hotmart charges 9.9% plus a fixed USD/EUR 1.00 per sale (no monthly fee) and handles checkout, local payment methods and installments.

payout.minimumPayout: A minimum applies; amount set in the Help Center (not confirmed)
payout.frequency: on request after 30-day release (or automatic monthly transfer)
payout.notes: Hotmart's payments policy: 9.9% service fee plus a fixed USD 1.00 / EUR 1.00 / BRL 2.49 per sale (20% and no fixed fee on products up to BRL 10). Balances are released 30 days after payment approval by default; eligible creators outside Brazil can take a paid cash advance within 2 business days. Each manual withdrawal has a fee and a minimum amount, given only in the Help Center, which could not be read. Automatic monthly transfers carry no withdrawal fee. Transactions are in BRL (Brazil), EUR (EU) or USD (everyone else).

legality.notes: Selling courses is legal everywhere. Courses on regulated topics (finance, health) need care to avoid unlicensed advice.
complianceRequirements: consumer-law refund rules (Hotmart offers a guarantee period)

availability.notes: Strong in Brazil, Spanish-speaking LATAM and Europe. Hotmart publishes no list of payout countries; withdrawals go to a bank account in your own name.

automationPlan: AI-drafted course scripts, slides and sales page
Affiliate swipe files and email sequences generated once
Automated checkout and member-area delivery
fullCycle: Upload course and set price and commission
risks: Affiliates may use aggressive marketing that hurts your brand
Withdrawal fee and minimum not published in the policy text
evidence: Hotmart is one of the largest course platforms in LATAM. Its pricing page confirms per-sale fees with no monthly fee, and its payments policy sets out the 9.9% + fixed fee and the 30-day release.

tools: Hotmart members area and checkout (no monthly fee)
LLM for scripts and sales page copy
skills: course design and recording (AI covers drafts)

unitEconomics.notes: Hotmart fee 9.9% + $1 per sale. Cost assumes about half of sales come via affiliates at ~50% commission (about $12.50) plus the $1 fixed fee. Typical LatAm infoproduct prices $20-200.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; the course takes 1-2 months to build and affiliates rarely promote a product with no sales history.

marketConditions.notes: Hotmart's affiliate marketplace is crowded with courses; top affiliates pick products with proven conversion and high commissions. Producers with their own audience win; newcomers rarely get affiliate traffic. AI makes course creation cheap, flooding the market and pushing buyers toward free AI tutoring. Failure modes: zero affiliate interest, refunds within the guarantee window.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch a low-ticket course ($20-30) with a generous 50-60% affiliate commission to attract promoters, then add a higher-priced tier or upsell once conversion data exists.
profitPath: Month 0-1: build a 1-2 hour course and sales page (cost $0)
Month 2-3: first sales from own network, $50-200 total
Month 3-6: list in affiliate marketplace, recruit 5-10 affiliates; $50-300/month
Month 6-12: optimise funnel, add upsell; most stay under $100/month, top cases $1k+

name: Freelance instructional design and e-learning module building for companies
summary: Build training courses (SCORM modules, onboarding courses, quizzes) for companies' Learning & Development teams as a freelancer.
howItWorks: Companies, NGOs and course creators need their knowledge turned into structured training: learning objectives, storyboards, interactive modules (Articulate Rise/Storyline, iSpring) and assessments exported as SCORM for their LMS. You take fixed-price projects on Upwork or win direct clients. LLMs draft outlines, scripts, quiz banks and voiceovers, and you design, QA and package. The payer is a business, not a learner, so budgets are larger than tutoring rates.

payout.minimumPayout: Upwork: USD 1+ PayPal / varies by method
payout.notes: Upwork releases fixed-price milestones after a 5-day security period and charges a variable 0-15% fee.

availability.notes: Upwork pays out almost everywhere in the reference set. Authoring tools such as Articulate have trials, and free tools (Adapt, H5P) work too.

automationPlan: LLM storyboard and script generation
AI voiceover and quiz-bank drafting
Template SCORM packages reused across clients
evidence: Upwork lists instructional design and e-learning development as standing categories with ongoing job posts. Corporate training is a large market.

tools: free authoring: Adapt Learning, H5P, iSpring Free (Articulate 360 optional, ~$1,000+/yr)
accounts: Stripe or Wise for direct invoices

unitEconomics.notes: Upwork instructional-design rates mostly $25-100/hr; Upwork fee is 0-15% (10% used). Cost covers Connects and AI credits per hour billed. Upwork's variable fee is estimated at 10% (official fee page bot-blocked).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurring $20/mo (startup cash not amortised). One or two billed hours a month covers the $20 AI subscription; break-even in months means first paid milestone, typically 1-3 months.

marketConditions.notes: Companies still buy SCORM modules and training rewrites, and specialists with portfolios in compliance, software onboarding or healthcare win. AI tools have made storyboards and voiceovers fast, so clients expect lower prices and generalist low-end gigs are shrinking. Failure modes: no portfolio, scope creep on fixed-price projects, and expensive authoring licenses. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $600 to $80 so it agrees with the 30% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Win first clients with fixed-price small modules ($200-500) using free tools, then quote per finished minute or per project at $40-70/hr equivalent once you have 3-5 portfolio pieces.
profitPath: Month 0: portfolio of 2 sample modules, Upwork profile (cost $50)
Month 1-2: first small project, $200-500
Month 3-6: 2-3 repeat clients, $500-1,500/month
Month 6-12: direct retainers and higher rates; $800-3,000/month for those who stick

name: Independent online tutoring practice with your own booking and payments
summary: Run tutoring under your own brand with your own booking page, payment links and local SEO, keeping 100% minus card fees.
howItWorks: Instead of paying a marketplace commission, you get students through a Google Business Profile, a simple site, school/parent networks and referrals. Then you sell lesson packages through a booking tool (Cal.com/Calendly or tutoring software like TutorBird/Teachworks) with Stripe or PayPal checkout. Packages paid in advance make income steady and cut no-shows. Marketplaces can still be a lead source, but repeat students stay direct where terms allow. Note that Preply and italki forbid moving their students off-platform.

payout.notes: Stripe pays out on a 2-7 day rolling schedule where supported. Elsewhere use PayPal or Wise invoices.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere. You may need to register as a sole trader; some countries require child-safeguarding checks for tutoring minors.
complianceRequirements: do not poach students from marketplaces that forbid it

availability.notes: Stripe is unavailable in parts of the reference list (e.g. several African and South Asian countries); PayPal/Wise cover most of the gaps.

automationPlan: Automated booking, reminders and package renewals
AI lesson plans, homework and progress reports
Review-request and referral emails
fullCycle: Publish Google Business Profile and site
Teach first students and get referrals
risks: Slow client acquisition without a marketplace
evidence: Many independent tutors run direct practices. Tutoring-software vendors (TutorBird, Teachworks) exist because of this market.

unitEconomics.notes: Private online tutoring rates of $20-80/hour (estimate from local market rates); cost is Stripe/PayPal processing (~3% + $0.30). No marketplace commission.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. Startup cash is the domain/site; one or two lessons recover it.

marketConditions.notes: Tutors with a niche (exam prep, specific curricula, adult professionals) and referral networks keep full schedules; generic homework help faces AI substitutes. Acquisition is slower than on a marketplace, but every lesson keeps ~97%. Failure modes: no inbound leads for months, no-shows without prepaid packages. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $400 to $80 so it agrees with the 35% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start near the local marketplace median with a free 20-minute consultation, sell prepaid 5- and 10-lesson packages, and raise rates for new students every 6 months once the schedule is full.
profitPath: Month 0: site, booking page, Google profile, tell school and parent networks (cost $20)
Month 1-2: first 2-3 students via referrals, $150-400/month
Month 3-6: 6-10 regular students, $400-1,000/month
Month 6-12: waitlist, higher rates, small groups; $500-2,000/month
